name: Anthony Chabot Campground
reservation_method: Park office (not reservations): (510) 690-6676, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4502
nightly_entry_cutoff: 10:00 PM -- the brochure states campground gates close at 10:00pm, and the park page gives campground and group camp gate hours as 8am-10pm, so there is no entry before 8am either. Stated by the agency, unlike Del Valle's cutoff, which is a visitor's near-miss report.
fee_notes: Drive-in camping $35/night; hike-in camping $25/night; RV hook-up camping $45/night. Limited overflow parking $8/night/vehicle. RV sewage disposal $20/use ($20 per use for non-campers). Firewood $10/bundle and charcoal $15/bag are sold at the campground kiosk. Park accepts cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover. Fees subject to change.
notes: Open year-round, in a eucalyptus grove overlooking Lake Chabot. Spacious tent sites, disabled accessible sites and facilities, RV hookup sites with sewage, water and 30-amp electric at a MAXIMUM VEHICLE LENGTH OF 35 FEET, and hot showers. Reservations are recommended for tent camping, full hookup sites and the limited overflow parking. Registered campers park free at the Lake Chabot Marina. There is no day-use parking in the campground -- see the park brochure for where to park instead. Seven group camping areas are bookable separately and are not this row. Stay limit is 15 consecutive days and 30 total days a year with a 2-day break after the first 15, which matches Ordinance 38 s.400.3(b) rather than adding to it. EBRPD's own park page puts the campground 20 minutes from downtown Oakland. STILL UNCONFIRMED, carried over from web search and NOT stated by either source read here: the site composition of 75 sites split 53 drive-up tent / 12 RV / 10 hike-in / 1 group. The $25 hike-in rate does confirm that hike-in sites exist, so access_mode is not uniform here; the row is tagged drive_in for the sites you can park at.

name: Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay
park: Dumbarton Quarry Campground on the Bay
notes: Open year-round. Reported composition, unconfirmed: about 60 paved sites with water, sewer and 50 amp electrical hookups, taking tent, walk-in, bike and RV camping. THE PARK FIELD IS UNCONFIRMED and is set to this campground's own name because EBRPD lists it as a park in its own right, while the same listing describes it as located within Coyote Hills Regional Park -- which appears separately in that list with its own camping. Which unit governs entrance fees and gate hours here is exactly the kind of question this field is joined on, so it is flagged rather than decided. As with Anthony Chabot, every fact here is from web-search summaries rather than a page read firsthand.
